Pandemic growth model — NOT ['Simulating patient zero', 'Modeling the curve'] (documentary-narrator voice), YES ['Setting up the model', 'Running the calculation']. Cancer timeline — NOT ['Charting the battle ahead'], YES ['Laying out the stages']. If you have to ask whether it's serious, it is. Otherwise, have fun — reach for alliteration, puns, personification, wordplay, whatever lands in that language. Playful examples — revenue chart: ['Bribing bars to stand taller', 'Asking Q4 where it went']; kanban: ['Herding cards into columns', 'Dragging, dropping, not stopping'].

title.description: Short snake_case identifier for this visual. Must be specific and disambiguating — if the conversation has multiple visuals, this title alone should tell you which one is being referenced (e.g. 'q4_revenue_by_product_line' not 'chart', 'oauth_login_flow' not 'diagram'). Also used as the download filename, so no spaces or special characters.

widget_code.description: SVG or HTML code to render. For SVG: raw SVG code starting with <svg> tag, must use CSS variables for colors. Example: <svg viewBox="0 0 700 400" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg">...</svg>. For HTML: raw HTML content to render, do NOT include DOCTYPE, <html>, <head>, or <body> tags. Use CSS variables for theming. Keep background transparent and avoid top-level padding. Scripts are supported but execute after streaming completes.

entries.name: SendMessage
entries.description:
# SendMessage

Send a message to another agent.

```json
{"to": "researcher", "summary": "assign task 1", "message": "start on task #1"}
```

| `to` | |
|---|---|
| `"researcher"` | Teammate by name |
| `"main"` | The main conversation (background subagents only) |
| `"worker"` | Any agent from `ListAgents` — subagent, another local Claude session |
| `"worker [3fa9c1]"` | Same, plus its `[ref]` — only when a listing or an error shows one |

Your plain text output is NOT visible to other agents — to communicate, you MUST call this tool. Messages from teammates are delivered automatically; you don't check an inbox. Refer to agents by name — names keep working after an agent completes (a send resumes it from its transcript). Use the raw `agentId` (format `a...-...`) from its spawn result only when the agent has no name, or when a newer agent took the name (latest wins). When relaying, don't quote the original — it's already rendered to the user.

## Cross-session

Use `ListAgents` to discover targets. Every row leads with the agent's `name [ref]` — the name IS the address; there is no separate address syntax.

```json
{"to": "worker", "message": "check if tests pass over there"}
{"to": "worker [3fa9c1]", "message": "you, specifically"}
```

Send the bare name — a name that exactly matches one live agent or session (on this machine, on another machine, or in the cloud) delivers directly. Append the ` [ref]` only when the bare name is not enough — `ListAgents` shows two rows with it, or an error asks you to disambiguate (you typed only a prefix, or a session list could not be checked). A ref you did not just read from a listing or an error will not resolve, and if the same name also names an in-process agent, the bare name always wins — use the in-process one.

A listed peer is alive and will receive your message; messages enqueue and drain at the receiver's next tool round (its `ListAgents` row says whether it is busy or idle right now). A successful send means the message reached that session, not that its Claude read it: a session running in a different permission mode than yours holds cross-session messages for its user's approval (and may let them expire), and a session can refuse them outright — for a session on this machine a `[Cross-session delivery notice]` tells you when that happens (the tool result says when this session has no inbox for one to reach); for a Remote Control, cloud or Claude Desktop session nothing reports back, so never treat silence as agreement. content.content:
== gpu GPU request for a pod create. Carries the CUDA host constraints, which
live here rather than at the body's top level so they are
unrepresentable on a CPU pod.

  id | string | GPU type identifier | enum= None | def= None
  count | integer | Number of GPUs | enum= None | def= 1
  allowedCudaVersions | array | Acceptable CUDA versions for the host machine, as `major.minor`. Omit to accept any version. Matching is exact, so a version no machine reports yields | enum= None | def= None
  minCudaVersion | string | Lowest acceptable CUDA version for the host machine, as `major.minor`, compared numerically rather than as a decimal — so 12.11 is above 12.2. Use thi | enum= None | def= None

content.text:
The 25–30 hours was a wall-clock estimate up to your 9 PM Sunday target, not GPU time. I overstated what the pod would actually need to run.

**Time breakdown**

| Step | Pod time |
|---|---|
| Setup and 25 GB download | about 0.5 h |
| Every-frame reference on about 40 sample videos (full-precision YOLO on every frame) | about 0.7 h |
| **First version on all 50 files** (you need its time for write-up Q1) | **about 3–6 h**: it decodes every frame of 125 h of video with little parallelism |
| Speed-up work: build, test on samples, check the gates, repeat | about 4–6 h of active use |
| Final full run, plus damaged-file tests | about 1 h |
| **Total** | **about 10–14 h, or $9–12 on Secure** |

The rest of the 30 hours is idle time (my coding, your sleep), when the pod should be stopped.

**Why I wouldn't rent a faster GPU (H100 or 5090)**
- The graders time the code on a 4090. TensorRT engines and batch sizes are tuned per GPU, so tuning on an H100 produces numbers that don't carry over.
- The likely bottleneck is **CPU video decoding**, not the GPU. 125 h at about 30 fps is about 13.5 million frames to decode, and YOLO only needs a sample of them. A faster GPU wouldn't fix the slowest part.
- An H100 costs about 3× more, and HARDWARE.md and your write-up timings would describe a different machine from the one grading you.

**What matters more: vCPUs.** The grading machine has 32 threads. A pod with **24–32 vCPUs** behaves like it and decodes faster; with 16 vCPUs, the speed-up work would target the wrong bottleneck. So I'd ask for at least 24, and fall back to 16 if no host has more.

**Recommendation**
1. **One Secure 4090 at $0.89/h**, asking for at least 24 vCPU and 48 GB RAM. Stop it overnight, but only after the first-version full run finishes, since that run can happen while we're idle anyway.
2. **Optional, and worth it: a second, cheap Community 4090 at $0.34/h** used only for the first version's full timed run, about 4–6 h for roughly $2. That gives a clean Q1 timing, and it means I'm not blocked or skewing the timing by testing on the same GPU.

Expected total: about **$12–15**.

content.text:
Here's my understanding of what I'm here for.

**The task**
Build ALETHIA AI's "Video Indexing at Speed" take-home for your AI Engineering application. It's due **Sun 22 Nov 2026, 11:55 PM PKT**, and the aim is to have everything committed by about 9 PM. The script `python run.py --input <folder> --output results.jsonl` reads FineVideo Parquet files and runs YOLO11l (imgsz 640, conf ≥ 0.4, default letterbox and NMS, rotation applied). For every second of every video it writes which of person / car / dog / laptop / cell phone appear and how many people are visible. Damaged videos get error lines instead of crashing the run.

**What the brief asks for**
- **Correctness first:** compared with a model run on every frame, object F1 ≥ 0.95, people count exact on ≥ 85% of seconds and within 1 on ≥ 95%. Speed only counts if all three pass.
- **Then speed:** timed on their RTX 4090 / 32-thread / offline machine, on about 13 h of unseen, possibly damaged video.
- **Repo contents:** `run.py` plus modules, exact-pinned `requirements.txt`, a `README.md` with install, apt and prep commands, `results.jsonl.gz` for all 50 files, `HARDWARE.md`, `WRITEUP.md`, and `ai_chats/`.

**Your rules for me**
1. Never write, edit or check `WRITEUP.md` content. You write it yourself. I keep only factual numbers in `NOTES.md`.
2. No secrets in files, commits or chat (HF token, RunPod key). Scan for tokens before every push.
3. Do the heavy work on a RunPod 4090, not this Mac. Remind you to stop the pod when it's idle. With the API key, show you the spec and price and **wait for your OK** before creating a pod.
4. Keep the repo private until you say to make it public. Send no email.
5. At the end, copy this project's Claude Code `.jsonl` chats into `ai_chats/` unedited (tokens become `[REMOVED]`), and show you the list before pushing.

**The goals behind it**
- Pass the gates with margin, because their test set includes damaged and unusual files.
- Be fast on *their* hardware, which is why I'm tuning on a 4090 with a similar vCPU count.
- Leave you a clear factual trail (first vs final timing, the change that saved the most time, where the time goes, how correctness was checked), so you can write the answers and explain the code on the 15-minute call.
- Keep the AI history honest and complete, since a missing or edited history counts against you.
- Keep cost sensible.

**Where it stands:** the scaffold is pushed to the private repo, and the RunPod key works. I'm waiting for your choice of pod setup before creating anything.

content.text:
**Why Hugging Face:** the FineVideo dataset is gated. You can only download it from an account that has accepted its terms, so the `hf download` of the 50 files (about 25 GB) needs your logged-in token. The model weights don't need it; `yolo11l.pt` comes from GitHub.

**What you can do now, before the pod exists:**
1. Open huggingface.co/datasets/HuggingFaceFV/finevideo and **accept the terms**, if you haven't already. Approval can take a moment, so this is the part worth doing early.
2. Create a **read** token at huggingface.co/settings/tokens.

**The login itself** has to end up on the pod, because that's where the download runs. Two ways:
- **On the pod (the plan):** once the pod is up, I give you the SSH command, and you run `hf auth login` there and paste the token. That takes about 1 minute.
- **Right now on this Mac:** you run `hf auth login` in your own terminal, which saves the token to `~/.cache/huggingface/token`. When the pod is up I copy that file over with `scp` and never print it. The token stays out of this chat and the repo, and you don't need to touch the pod at all. The catch is that I'd be handling the token file, which is different from what you originally said.

If you choose the second way, this installs the `hf` command on the Mac (a few MB):

pip3 install --user -U huggingface_hub

"""Survey the videos: codec, size, fps, duration, rotation, B-frames, row groups.

python tools/inspect_data.py --input finevideo/data --out survey.csv
"""
import argparse
import csv
import io
import os
import sys
from multiprocessing import Pool

import av
import pyarrow.parquet as pq

sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))))
from vidx.parquet_io import iter_videos, list_parquet  # noqa: E402


def probe(path):
    rows = []
    pf = pq.ParquetFile(path)
    groups = pf.num_row_groups
    for vid, data, err in iter_videos(path):
        r = dict(video=vid, row_groups=groups, bytes=len(data or b""), error=err or "")
        if data:
            try:
                with av.open(io.BytesIO(data)) as c:
                    s = c.streams.video[0]
                    cc = s.codec_context
                    r.update(codec=cc.name, width=cc.width, height=cc.height,
                             pix_fmt=cc.format.name if cc.format else "",
                             avg_rate=float(s.average_rate or 0),
                             frames=s.frames,
                             duration=float(s.duration * s.time_base) if s.duration else
                             (c.duration / 1e6 if c.duration else 0),
                             has_b=getattr(cc, "has_b_frames", ""),
                             rotate=(s.metadata or {}).get("rotate", ""))
                    f = next(c.decode(s))
                    r["frame_rotation"] = getattr(f, "rotation", "")
            except Exception as e:
                r["error"] = f"{type(e).__name__}: {e}"[:100]
        rows.append(r)
    return rows


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--input", required=True)
    ap.add_argument("--out", required=True)
    ap.add_argument("--workers", type=int, default=12)
    args = ap.parse_args()
    with Pool(args.workers) as p:
        allrows = [r for rows in p.map(probe, list_parquet(args.input)) for r in rows]
    keys = sorted({k for r in allrows for k in r})
    with open(args.out, "w", newline="") as f:
        w = csv.DictWriter(f, keys)
        w.writeheader()
        w.writerows(allrows)
    print(f"{len(allrows)} videos -> {args.out}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

"""Survey the videos: codec, size, fps, duration, rotation, B-frames, row groups.

python tools/inspect_data.py --input finevideo/data --out survey.csv
"""
import argparse
import csv
import io
import os
import sys
from multiprocessing import Pool

import av
import pyarrow.parquet as pq

sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))))
from vidx.parquet_io import iter_videos, list_parquet  # noqa: E402


def probe(path):
    rows = []
    pf = pq.ParquetFile(path)
    groups = pf.num_row_groups
    for vid, data, err in iter_videos(path):
        r = dict(video=vid, row_groups=groups, bytes=len(data or b""), error=err or "")
        if data:
            try:
                with av.open(io.BytesIO(data)) as c:
                    s = c.streams.video[0]
                    cc = s.codec_context
                    r.update(codec=cc.name, width=cc.width, height=cc.height,
                             pix_fmt=cc.format.name if cc.format else "",
                             avg_rate=float(s.average_rate or 0),
                             frames=s.frames,
                             duration=float(s.duration * s.time_base) if s.duration else
                             (c.duration / 1e6 if c.duration else 0),
                             has_b=getattr(cc, "has_b_frames", ""),
                             rotate=(s.metadata or {}).get("rotate", ""))
                    f = next(c.decode(s))
                    r["frame_rotation"] = getattr(f, "rotation", "")
            except Exception as e:
                r["error"] = f"{type(e).__name__}: {e}"[:100]
        rows.append(r)
    return rows


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--input", required=True)
    ap.add_argument("--out", required=True)
    ap.add_argument("--workers", type=int, default=12)
    args = ap.parse_args()
    with Pool(args.workers) as p:
        allrows = [r for rows in p.map(probe, list_parquet(args.input)) for r in rows]
    keys = sorted({k for r in allrows for k in r})
    with open(args.out, "w", newline="") as f:
        w = csv.DictWriter(f, keys)
        w.writeheader()
        w.writerows(allrows)
    print(f"{len(allrows)} videos -> {args.out}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

"""Decode throughput: threads vs processes, skip_frame, frame conversion cost.

python tools/bench_decode.py --input finevideo/data --n 12 --workers 1 4 8 12 16
"""
import argparse
import io
import os
import sys
import time
from concurrent.futures import ProcessPoolExecutor, ThreadPoolExecutor

import av

sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))))
from vidx.parquet_io import iter_videos, list_parquet  # noqa: E402

VIDEOS = []


def decode(i, skip="DEFAULT", convert_every=0, threads=1):
    data = VIDEOS[i]
    n = 0
    with av.open(io.BytesIO(data)) as c:
        s = c.streams.video[0]
        s.codec_context.skip_frame = skip
        if threads > 1:
            s.thread_type = "AUTO"
            s.thread_count = threads
        for f in c.decode(s):
            if convert_every and n % convert_every == 0:
                f.to_ndarray(format="bgr24")
            n += 1
    return n


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--input", required=True)
    ap.add_argument("--n", type=int, default=12)
    ap.add_argument("--workers", type=int, nargs="+", default=[1, 4, 8, 12, 16])
    args = ap.parse_args()
    for vid, data, err in iter_videos(list_parquet(args.input)[0]):
        if data:
            VIDEOS.append(data)
        if len(VIDEOS) >= args.n:
            break
    idx = list(range(len(VIDEOS)))

    def run(pool_cls, w, **kw):
        t = time.time()
        with pool_cls(w) as p:
            n = sum(p.map(_call, [(i, kw) for i in idx]))
        return n / (time.time() - t)

    n1 = decode(0)
    t = time.time(); decode(0); single = n1 / (time.time() - t)
    t = time.time(); decode(0, skip="NONREF"); nonref = n1 / (time.time() - t)
    t = time.time(); decode(0, convert_every=1); conv = n1 / (time.time() - t)

"""Letterbox geometry identical to Ultralytics' LetterBox(auto=True, stride=32).

Ultralytics' predictor uses auto=True (minimum-rectangle padding) when all
images in a batch have the same shape and the model is a PyTorch model, which
is how the reference is produced. A 640x360 frame therefore becomes 640x384
(no resize, 12 px of grey padding top and bottom).
"""
import cv2
import numpy as np

PAD = 114


def geometry(h, w, imgsz=640, stride=32):
    """Return (out_h, out_w, new_h, new_w, top, left) for an h x w frame."""
    r = min(imgsz / h, imgsz / w)
    new_w, new_h = int(round(w * r)), int(round(h * r))
    dw, dh = imgsz - new_w, imgsz - new_h
    dw, dh = np.mod(dw, stride), np.mod(dh, stride)
    dw, dh = dw / 2, dh / 2
    top, bottom = int(round(dh - 0.1)), int(round(dh + 0.1))
    left, right = int(round(dw - 0.1)), int(round(dw + 0.1))
    return new_h + top + bottom, new_w + left + right, new_h, new_w, top, left


def letterbox_into(img, dst, geom):
    """Write the letterboxed `img` into `dst` (out_h x out_w x 3, uint8).

    `dst` must already hold the grey padding outside the image area; only the
    image area is written.
    """
    _, _, new_h, new_w, top, left = geom
    h, w = img.shape[:2]
    view = dst[top:top + new_h, left:left + new_w]
    if (h, w) == (new_h, new_w):
        view[...] = img
    else:
        cv2.resize(img, (new_w, new_h), dst=view, interpolation=cv2.INTER_LINEAR)

"""GPU post-processing equivalent to Ultralytics' non_max_suppression for our use.

Ultralytics (multi_label=False) gives each candidate box its single best class
over all 80 classes, keeps it if that score > conf, then runs class-aware NMS
(IoU 0.7). Restricting to our five classes after the arg-max (as its
`classes=` argument does) does not change the five classes' results, because
NMS never compares boxes of different classes.

We only need the number of surviving boxes per class per image.
"""
import torch
import torchvision

from . import CLASS_IDS, CONF, IOU

MAX_NMS = 30000  # Ultralytics defaults
MAX_DET = 300


def count_classes(pred, conf=CONF, iou=IOU):
    """pred: (B, 4 + 80, N) raw YOLO output -> int32 tensor (B, 5) on GPU."""
    B = pred.shape[0]
    device = pred.device
    cls_ids = torch.tensor(CLASS_IDS, device=device)
    p = pred.transpose(1, 2)  # (B, N, 84)
    scores, labels = p[..., 4:].max(-1)  # best class per box
    keep = (scores > conf) & torch.isin(labels, cls_ids)
    b_idx, a_idx = keep.nonzero(as_tuple=True)
    out = torch.zeros((B, len(CLASS_IDS)), dtype=torch.int32, device=device)
    if b_idx.numel() == 0:
        return out
    boxes = p[b_idx, a_idx, :4].float()
    xy, wh = boxes[:, :2], boxes[:, 2:] / 2
    boxes = torch.cat((xy - wh, xy + wh), 1)  # xywh -> xyxy
    sc = scores[b_idx, a_idx].float()
    lab = labels[b_idx, a_idx]
    # Ultralytics keeps at most MAX_NMS candidates per image (by score); with
    # conf 0.4 and five classes this never binds, so we do not emulate it.
    group = b_idx * 80 + lab
    kept = torchvision.ops.batched_nms(boxes, sc, group, iou)
    kb, kl = b_idx[kept], lab[kept]
    # MAX_DET per image: also never binds in practice for 5 classes.
    col = torch.searchsorted(cls_ids, kl)
    out.index_put_((kb, col), torch.ones_like(kb, dtype=torch.int32), accumulate=True)
    return out

"""GPU post-processing equivalent to Ultralytics' non_max_suppression for our use.

Ultralytics (multi_label=False) gives each candidate box its single best class
over all 80 classes, keeps it if that score > conf, then runs class-aware NMS
(IoU 0.7). Restricting to our five classes after the arg-max (as its
`classes=` argument does) does not change the five classes' results, because
NMS never compares boxes of different classes.

We only need the number of surviving boxes per class per image.
"""
import torch
import torchvision

from . import CLASS_IDS, CONF, IOU

MAX_NMS = 30000  # Ultralytics defaults
MAX_DET = 300


def count_classes(pred, conf=CONF, iou=IOU):
    """pred: (B, 4 + 80, N) raw YOLO output -> int32 tensor (B, 5) on GPU."""
    B = pred.shape[0]
    device = pred.device
    cls_ids = torch.tensor(CLASS_IDS, device=device)
    p = pred.transpose(1, 2)  # (B, N, 84)
    scores, labels = p[..., 4:].max(-1)  # best class per box
    keep = (scores > conf) & torch.isin(labels, cls_ids)
    b_idx, a_idx = keep.nonzero(as_tuple=True)
    out = torch.zeros((B, len(CLASS_IDS)), dtype=torch.int32, device=device)
    if b_idx.numel() == 0:
        return out
    boxes = p[b_idx, a_idx, :4].float()
    xy, wh = boxes[:, :2], boxes[:, 2:] / 2
    boxes = torch.cat((xy - wh, xy + wh), 1)  # xywh -> xyxy
    sc = scores[b_idx, a_idx].float()
    lab = labels[b_idx, a_idx]
    # Ultralytics keeps at most MAX_NMS candidates per image (by score); with
    # conf 0.4 and five classes this never binds, so we do not emulate it.
    group = b_idx * 80 + lab
    kept = torchvision.ops.batched_nms(boxes, sc, group, iou)
    kb, kl = b_idx[kept], lab[kept]
    # MAX_DET per image: also never binds in practice for 5 classes.
    col = torch.searchsorted(cls_ids, kl)
    out.index_put_((kb, col), torch.ones_like(kb, dtype=torch.int32), accumulate=True)
    return out

"""YOLO11l inference backends returning the raw (B, 84, N) prediction tensor.

- TensorRT FP16 engine (built once by prepare.py on the target GPU), with a

- PyTorch fallback (Ultralytics model, FP16) if the engine is missing or
  TensorRT cannot load it.

import os

import torch

MAX_BATCH = 64
OPT_HW = (384, 640)


def export_onnx(weights, onnx_path):
    from ultralytics import YOLO

    out = YOLO(weights).export(format="onnx", dynamic=True, imgsz=640, simplify=True,
                               opset=17, verbose=False)
    if os.path.abspath(out) != os.path.abspath(onnx_path):
        os.replace(out, onnx_path)
    return onnx_path


def build_engine(onnx_path, engine_path, max_batch=MAX_BATCH, opt_hw=OPT_HW):
    import tensorrt as trt

    logger = trt.Logger(trt.Logger.WARNING)
    builder = trt.Builder(logger)
    network = builder.create_network(0)
    parser = trt.OnnxParser(network, logger)
    with open(onnx_path, "rb") as f:
        if not parser.parse(f.read()):
            errs = [str(parser.get_error(i)) for i in range(parser.num_errors)]
            raise RuntimeError("ONNX parse failed: " + "; ".join(errs))
    config = builder.create_builder_config()
    config.set_memory_pool_limit(trt.MemoryPoolType.WORKSPACE, 8 << 30)
    config.set_flag(trt.BuilderFlag.FP16)
    inp = network.get_input(0)
    profile = builder.create_optimization_profile()
    profile.set_shape(inp.name, (1, 3, 32, 32), (max_batch, 3, *opt_hw),
                      (max_batch, 3, 640, 640))
    config.add_optimization_profile(profile)
    data = builder.build_serialized_network(network, config)
    if data is None:
        raise RuntimeError("TensorRT engine build failed")
    with open(engine_path, "wb") as f:
        f.write(data)
    return engine_path


class TRTModel:
    def __init__(self, engine_path, device="cuda:0"):
        import tensorrt as trt

        self.trt = trt
        self.device = torch.device(device)
        logger = trt.Logger(trt.Logger.WARNING)
        with open(engine_path, "rb") as f:
            self.engine = trt.Runtime(logger).deserialize_cuda_engine(f.read())
        if self.engine is None:
            raise RuntimeError("could not deserialize TensorRT engine")
        self.ctx = self.engine.create_execution_context()
        names = [self.engine.get_tensor_name(i) for i in range(self.engine.num_io_tensors)]
        self.inp = next(n for n in names
                        if self.engine.get_tensor_mode(n) == trt.TensorIOMode.INPUT)
        self.out = next(n for n in names
                        if self.engine.get_tensor_mode(n) == trt.TensorIOMode.OUTPUT)
        self.in_dtype = torch.float16 if self.engine.get_tensor_dtype(self.inp) == trt.float16 \
            else torch.float32
        self.out_dtype = torch.float16 if self.engine.get_tensor_dtype(self.out) == trt.float16 \
            else torch.float32
        self.max_batch = self.engine.get_tensor_profile_shape(self.inp, 0)[2][0]
        self.stream = torch.cuda.Stream(self.device)

    def __call__(self, x):
        x = x.to(self.in_dtype).contiguous()
        self.ctx.set_input_shape(self.inp, tuple(x.shape))
        out = torch.empty(tuple(self.ctx.get_tensor_shape(self.out)), dtype=self.out_dtype,
                          device=self.device)
        self.ctx.set_tensor_address(self.inp, x.data_ptr())
        self.ctx.set_tensor_address(self.out, out.data_ptr())
        cur = torch.cuda.current_stream(self.device)
        self.stream.wait_stream(cur)
        self.ctx.execute_async_v3(self.stream.cuda_stream)
        cur.wait_stream(self.stream)
        return out


class TorchModel:
    def __init__(self, weights, device="cuda:0", half=True):
        from ultralytics import YOLO

        self.device = torch.device(device)
        self.half = half
        m = YOLO(weights).model.to(self.device).eval()
        m = m.fuse() if hasattr(m, "fuse") else m
        self.model = m.half() if half else m.float()
        self.max_batch = MAX_BATCH

    @torch.inference_mode()
    def __call__(self, x):
        x = x.half() if self.half else x.float()
        y = self.model(x)
        return y[0] if isinstance(y, (list, tuple)) else y


def load_model(weights, engine_path, log=print):
    if engine_path and os.path.exists(engine_path):
        try:
            m = TRTModel(engine_path)
            log(f"backend: TensorRT engine {engine_path}")
            return m
        except Exception as e:  # fall back rather than fail the run
            log(f"TensorRT unavailable ({type(e).__name__}: {e}); using PyTorch FP16")
    else:
        log("backend: PyTorch FP16 (no TensorRT engine found)")
    return TorchModel(weights)

1. Downloads the official yolo11l.pt weights next to run.py.
2. Exports them to ONNX and builds a TensorRT FP16 engine for this GPU
   (yolo11l.engine). If this step fails, run.py falls back to PyTorch FP16.

import os
import sys
import time
import urllib.request

HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
URL = "https://github.com/ultralytics/assets/releases/download/v8.3.0/yolo11l.pt"

    weights = os.path.join(HERE, "yolo11l.pt")
    if not os.path.exists(weights):
        print(f"downloading {URL}")
        urllib.request.urlretrieve(URL, weights + ".part")
        os.replace(weights + ".part", weights)
    print(f"weights: {weights} ({os.path.getsize(weights) / 1e6:.1f} MB)")

    sys.path.insert(0, HERE)
    from vidx.engine import build_engine, export_onnx

    onnx_path = os.path.join(HERE, "yolo11l.onnx")
    engine_path = os.path.join(HERE, "yolo11l.engine")
    t = time.time()
    if not os.path.exists(onnx_path):
        export_onnx(weights, onnx_path)
    print(f"onnx: {onnx_path}")
    build_engine(onnx_path, engine_path + ".part")
    os.replace(engine_path + ".part", engine_path)
    print(f"engine: {engine_path} ({time.time() - t:.0f}s)")

    main()

input.content:
"""Compare backends on identical frames and time the GPU path.

- per-frame count agreement: Ultralytics predict (FP32, the reference path)
  vs our letterbox + TensorRT FP16 + GPU NMS, and vs PyTorch FP16.
- throughput of the TensorRT engine at several batch sizes.

python tools/bench_gpu.py --input finevideo/data --frames 1024
"""
import argparse
import os
import sys
import time

import numpy as np
import torch

sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))))
from vidx.detect_ultra import UltralyticsDetector  # noqa: E402
from vidx.engine import TorchModel, TRTModel  # noqa: E402
from vidx.letterbox import PAD, geometry, letterbox_into  # noqa: E402
from vidx.parquet_io import iter_videos, list_parquet  # noqa: E402
from vidx.postprocess import count_classes  # noqa: E402
from vidx.video import VideoReader  # noqa: E402

HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))


def to_input(batch_u8):
    x = torch.from_numpy(batch_u8).cuda()
    return x.permute(0, 3, 1, 2).flip(1).float().div_(255)


def ours(model, frames, bs=64):
    out = []
    for i in range(0, len(frames), bs):
        chunk = frames[i:i + bs]
        h, w = chunk[0].shape[:2]
        g = geometry(h, w)
        buf = np.full((len(chunk), g[0], g[1], 3), PAD, np.uint8)
        for j, f in enumerate(chunk):
            letterbox_into(f, buf[j], g)
        out.append(count_classes(model(to_input(buf))).cpu().numpy())
    return np.concatenate(out)


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--input", required=True)
    ap.add_argument("--frames", type=int, default=1024)
    ap.add_argument("--file", type=int, default=3)
    args = ap.parse_args()
    frames = []
    for vid, data, err in iter_videos(list_parquet(args.input)[args.file]):
        if not data:
            continue
        for _, img in VideoReader(data, per_second=3):
            frames.append(img)
        if len(frames) >= args.frames:
            break
    frames = frames[: args.frames]
    shapes = {f.shape for f in frames}
    print(f"{len(frames)} frames, shapes {shapes}")
    # group by shape so every batch has one shape (as in Ultralytics' rect mode)
    by_shape = {}
    for f in frames:
        by_shape.setdefault(f.shape, []).append(f)
    frames = [f for fs in by_shape.values() for f in fs]

    ref = np.concatenate([UltralyticsDetector(os.path.join(HERE, "yolo11l.pt")).counts(fs)
                          for fs in by_shape.values()])
    trt_model = TRTModel(os.path.join(HERE, "yolo11l.engine"))
    a = np.concatenate([ours(trt_model, fs) for fs in by_shape.values()])
    tm = TorchModel(os.path.join(HERE, "yolo11l.pt"), half=True)
    b = np.concatenate([ours(tm, fs) for fs in by_shape.values()])
    tm32 = TorchModel(os.path.join(HERE, "yolo11l.pt"), half=False)
    c = np.concatenate([ours(tm32, fs) for fs in by_shape.values()])
    for name, x in [("TRT fp16", a), ("torch fp16", b), ("torch fp32 (our pre/post)", c)]:
        same = (x == ref).all(1).mean()
        print(f"{name:28s}: frames identical to Ultralytics {same:.4f}, "
              f"per-class mismatches {(x != ref).sum(0).tolist()}, "
              f"totals {x.sum(0).tolist()} vs {ref.sum(0).tolist()}")

    # throughput, synthetic input at 384x640
    for bs in (16, 32, 64):
        x = torch.rand(bs, 3, 384, 640, device="cuda")
        for _ in range(3):
            count_classes(trt_model(x))
        torch.cuda.synchronize()
        n = 30
        t = time.time()
        for _ in range(n):
            count_classes(trt_model(x)).cpu()
        torch.cuda.synchronize()
        print(f"TRT bs={bs}: {bs * n / (time.time() - t):.0f} fps (384x640, incl. NMS)")
    x = torch.rand(64, 3, 384, 640, device="cuda")
    tm(x)
    torch.cuda.synchronize()
    t = time.time()
    for _ in range(10):
        count_classes(tm(x)).cpu()
    print(f"torch fp16 bs=64: {640 / (time.time() - t):.0f} fps")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

# Engineering log

Plain record of what was run, what changed, and the measured numbers.
Times are wall-clock on the RunPod pod described in HARDWARE.md unless noted.
"Gates" = brief section 5: object F1 >= 0.95, people exact >= 85%, within 1 >= 95%.

## Pod

- RunPod Secure cloud, RTX 4090 24 GB, driver 595.112.07, AMD EPYC 7452
  (container CPU quota 13.6 cores, 16 vCPU allocated), 1 TB host RAM visible
  (125 GB allocated), Ubuntu 22.04.5, Python 3.11.10. Created 21 Nov 12:54 PKT.
- Dataset download (`hf download ... train-000[0-4]*`): 50 files, 24 GB, 31 s.

## Data survey (tools/inspect_data.py, all 50 files)

- 1,650 videos, 128.0 hours, 12,981,615 frames. 0 videos failed to open.
- Codec: H.264 for all 1,650; pixel format yuv420p for all.
- Sizes: 640x360 = 1,284; 360x640 (portrait) = 141; 480x360 = 49; 270x480 = 31;
  202x360 = 28; others < 10 each. Largest dimension is 640 everywhere.
- Frame rates: 29.97 = 575, 30 = 505, 25 = 265, 23.98 = 177, 24 = 71, plus a few
  at 7-15 fps.
- Rotation tags: none in these 50 files.
- B-frames present in 1,376 of 1,650 videos.
- Each Parquet file is a single row group (~500 MB).
- Duration per video: 19 s to 658 s, median 242 s.

## Checks on synthetic inputs

- Rotation: test video tagged 90/180/270 degrees. Our PyAV frames after rotation
  are pixel-identical (mean abs diff 0.0) to OpenCV's auto-rotated frames and
  to ffmpeg CLI output.
- Damaged inputs (first version): unreadable Parquet file, truncated mp4, random
  bytes, empty bytes, null row -> one error line each, run continues.

## Reference (tools/reference.py)

- 59 videos sampled (44 random + portrait, odd sizes, low fps, no-B-frame cases),
  4.15 hours, 412,151 frames, 14,958 seconds.
- Plain Ultralytics predict, FP32, every frame. 3 processes sharing the GPU,
  ~300 frames/s total, ~25 min.

## Sampling simulation (tools/simulate.py, reference per-frame counts)

Frames analysed per second (K), taking the first frame in each 1/K-second slot,
aggregated with the brief's rules, scored against all frames:

| K | frames used | F1 | exact | within 1 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 3.6% | 0.9528 | 0.8954 | 0.9811 |
| 2 | 7.3% | 0.9654 | 0.9241 | 0.9952 |
| 3 | 10.9% | 0.9826 | 0.9502 | 0.9968 |
| 4 | 14.5% | 0.9828 | 0.9551 | 0.9989 |
| 5 | 18.1% | 0.9891 | 0.9673 | 0.9985 |
| 6 | 21.7% | 0.9886 | 0.9690 | 0.9994 |
| 8 | 28.9% | 0.9919 | 0.9758 | 0.9997 |
| 10 | 36.1% | 0.9936 | 0.9801 | 1.0000 |
| 15 | 53.8% | 0.9967 | 0.9899 | 0.9998 |

## Micro-benchmarks

- Decode (PyAV, 360p H.264, one core): ~2,100 frames/s; with skip_frame=NONREF
  (B-frames skipped) a video is processed ~1.8x faster. +bgr24 conversion of
  every frame: ~1,600 frames/s.
- Decode in parallel (24 videos): 4 processes 6,856 fps; 8 processes 11,466 fps;
  12 processes 14,611 fps. Threads: 8 -> 10,493 fps, 12 -> 9,468 fps.
  (Measured while the reference used ~3 cores.)
- TensorRT 10.9 FP16 engine, dynamic shape optimised for 384x640, incl. GPU NMS:
  bs16 1,817 fps, bs32 1,989 fps, bs64 1,996 fps. PyTorch FP16 bs64: 921 fps.
  Engine build took 548 s (GPU shared with reference at the time).
- Same 1,024 frames, per-frame counts identical to Ultralytics FP32 predict:
  TensorRT FP16 99.41%, PyTorch FP16 99.80%, PyTorch FP32 with our own
  letterbox/NMS 99.90%.

## Runs

| Start (PKT) | Version | Data | Wall time | F1 | Exact | Within 1 | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 21 Nov 13:33 | v1-simple (tag), K=3, 1 process, Ultralytics FP32 bs32 | 50 files | running | | | | |

"""Decode worker process.

Each worker takes whole videos (mp4 bytes) from a task queue, decodes them
with PyAV on one core, keeps K frames per second (first frame in each
1/K-second slot), letterboxes them exactly like Ultralytics and writes them
into "chunks" in a shared-memory block owned by the main process. It then
sends a small message describing the chunk; the main process copies it to the
GPU and hands the chunk back through `free_q`.

Messages sent on `msg_q`:
  ("start", wid, vid)
  ("chunk", wid, chunk_id, vid, n, out_h, out_w, seconds)
  ("end", wid, vid, last_second, n_decoded, error_or_None)
"""
import io
import math
import os
import traceback
from fractions import Fraction

import numpy as np

SLOT_BYTES = 640 * 640 * 3  # max letterboxed frame


def worker_main(wid, task_q, msg_q, free_q, shm_name, n_chunks, chunk_frames, cfg):
    os.environ.setdefault("OMP_NUM_THREADS", "1")
    import av
    import cv2
    from multiprocessing import shared_memory

    from .letterbox import PAD, geometry
    from .video import _rotation_cw, rotate

    cv2.setNumThreads(1)
    av.logging.set_level(av.logging.PANIC)  # damaged files: no log spam
    shm = shared_memory.SharedMemory(name=shm_name)
    block = np.ndarray((n_chunks, chunk_frames * SLOT_BYTES), np.uint8, shm.buf)
    k = cfg["per_second"]
    skip_nonref = cfg.get("skip_nonref", False)

    while True:
        task = task_q.get()
        if task is None:
            break
        vid, data = task
        msg_q.put(("start", wid, vid))
        state = {"chunk": None, "view": None, "n": 0, "secs": [], "geom": None, "fill": None}

        def send_chunk():
            if state["chunk"] is not None and state["n"]:
                g = state["geom"]
                msg_q.put(("chunk", wid, state["chunk"], vid, state["n"], g[0], g[1],
                           state["secs"]))
            elif state["chunk"] is not None:
                free_q.put(state["chunk"])
            state.update(chunk=None, view=None, n=0, secs=[])

        def add_frame(sec, img):
            h, w = img.shape[:2]
            if state["geom"] is None or state["geom_hw"] != (h, w):
                send_chunk()  # shape changed: never mix shapes in one chunk
                state["geom"] = geometry(h, w)
                state["geom_hw"] = (h, w)
            g = state["geom"]
            out_h, out_w, new_h, new_w, top, left = g
            if state["chunk"] is None:
                cid = free_q.get()
                state["chunk"] = cid
                state["view"] = block[cid, : chunk_frames * out_h * out_w * 3].reshape(
                    chunk_frames, out_h, out_w, 3)
            dst = state["view"][state["n"]]
            # grey padding strips, then the image
            if top:
                dst[:top] = PAD
            if top + new_h < out_h:
                dst[top + new_h:] = PAD
            if left:
                dst[:, :left] = PAD
            if left + new_w < out_w:
                dst[:, left + new_w:] = PAD
            area = dst[top:top + new_h, left:left + new_w]
            if (h, w) == (new_h, new_w):
                area[...] = img
            else:
                area[...] = cv2.resize(img, (new_w, new_h), interpolation=cv2.INTER_LINEAR)
            state["secs"].append(sec)
            state["n"] += 1
            if state["n"] == chunk_frames:
                send_chunk()

        last_second, n_decoded, error = -1, 0, None
        try:
            container = av.open(io.BytesIO(data), mode="r", metadata_errors="ignore")
            try:
                if not container.streams.video:
                    raise ValueError("no video stream")
                stream = container.streams.video[0]
                cc = stream.codec_context
                if skip_nonref:
                    cc.skip_frame = "NONREF"
                tb = stream.time_base or Fraction(1, 1000)
                fps = float(stream.average_rate or stream.guessed_rate or 30)
                first_pts, max_pkt_pts, rot, last_slot = None, None, None, None
                for packet in container.demux(stream):
                    if packet.pts is not None and (max_pkt_pts is None or packet.pts > max_pkt_pts):
                        max_pkt_pts = packet.pts
                    for frame in packet.decode():
                        idx = n_decoded
                        n_decoded += 1
                        if frame.pts is not None:
                            if first_pts is None:
                                first_pts = frame.pts
                            t = (frame.pts - first_pts) * tb
                        else:
                            t = Fraction(idx) / Fraction(fps)
                        if t < 0:
                            t = Fraction(0)
                        sec = math.floor(t)
                        if sec > last_second:
                            last_second = sec
                        if k:
                            slot = (sec, math.floor((t - sec) * k))
                            if slot == last_slot:
                                continue
                            last_slot = slot
                        if rot is None:
                            rot = _rotation_cw(stream, frame)
                        img = frame.to_ndarray(format="bgr24")
                        add_frame(sec, rotate(img, rot))
                if skip_nonref and first_pts is not None and max_pkt_pts is not None:
                    # skipped B-frames may lie after the last decoded frame
                    last_second = max(last_second, math.floor((max_pkt_pts - first_pts) * tb))
            finally:
                container.close()
        except Exception as e:
            error = f"could not decode video: {type(e).__name__}"
            if cfg.get("debug"):
                traceback.print_exc()
        send_chunk()
        if n_decoded == 0 and error is None:
            error = "no frames decoded"
        msg_q.put(("end", wid, vid, last_second, n_decoded, error))
    shm.close()

input.content:
"""Fast pipeline: parallel decode workers -> shared memory -> one GPU loop.

Main process:
  - a reader thread reads Parquet files in order and puts (video id, mp4
    bytes) on the task queue (error rows go straight to the output);
  - N worker processes decode/sample/letterbox into shared-memory chunks;
  - the main thread batches chunks of the same shape, runs YOLO on the GPU,
    counts the five classes per frame, and writes each video's lines as soon
    as its last chunk is done;
  - a worker that dies (e.g. a decoder crash on a damaged file) is replaced,
    and its current video gets an error line.
"""
import json
import multiprocessing as mp
import os
import queue
import sys
import threading
import time
from multiprocessing import shared_memory

import numpy as np

from .aggregate import per_second
from .parquet_io import iter_videos, list_parquet
from .worker import SLOT_BYTES, worker_main


def log(*a):
    print(*a, file=sys.stderr, flush=True)


class Output:
    def __init__(self, path):
        self.f = open(path, "w")
        self.n_videos = 0

    def write(self, records):
        self.f.write("".join(json.dumps(r) + "\n" for r in records))
        self.n_videos += 1

    def close(self):
        self.f.close()


class VideoState:
    __slots__ = ("secs", "counts", "chunks_sent", "chunks_done", "end")

    def __init__(self):
        self.secs, self.counts = [], []
        self.chunks_sent = self.chunks_done = 0
        self.end = None  # (last_second, n_decoded, error)


def records_for(vid, st, extra_error=None):
    last_second, _, error = st.end
    error = error or extra_error
    recs = []
    if last_second >= 0:
        secs = np.concatenate(st.secs) if st.secs else np.zeros(0, np.int64)
        counts = np.concatenate(st.counts) if st.counts else np.zeros((0, 5), np.int32)
        for s, (objects, people) in enumerate(per_second(secs, counts, last_second)):
            recs.append({"video": vid, "second": s, "objects": objects, "people": people})
    if error:
        recs.append({"video": vid, "error": error})
    return recs


def run(input_dir, output_path, model, n_workers, per_second_k=3, skip_nonref=False,
        max_batch=64, chunk_frames=32, chunks_per_worker=4, debug=False):
    import torch

    from .postprocess import count_classes

    ctx = mp.get_context("fork")
    t0 = time.time()
    out = Output(output_path)
    cfg = {"per_second": per_second_k, "skip_nonref": skip_nonref, "debug": debug}
    task_q = ctx.Queue(maxsize=max(4, n_workers))
    msg_q = ctx.Queue()
    workers = {}  # wid -> dict(proc, free_q, shm, block, current)

    def start_worker(wid):
        shm = shared_memory.SharedMemory(create=True,
                                         size=chunks_per_worker * chunk_frames * SLOT_BYTES)
        block = np.ndarray((chunks_per_worker, chunk_frames * SLOT_BYTES), np.uint8, shm.buf)
        free_q = ctx.SimpleQueue()
        for c in range(chunks_per_worker):
            free_q.put(c)
        p = ctx.Process(target=worker_main, daemon=True,
                        args=(wid, task_q, msg_q, free_q, shm.name, chunks_per_worker,
                              chunk_frames, cfg))
        p.start()
        workers[wid] = dict(proc=p, free_q=free_q, shm=shm, block=block, current=None)

    for wid in range(n_workers):
        start_worker(wid)

    videos = {}  # vid -> VideoState
    reader_done = threading.Event()
    n_tasks = [0]
    direct_errors = queue.Queue()  # rows that failed before decoding

    def reader():
        try:
            for path in list_parquet(input_dir):
                for vid, data, err in iter_videos(path):
                    if err:
                        direct_errors.put({"video": vid, "error": err})
                        continue
                    n_tasks[0] += 1
                    task_q.put((vid, data))
                log(f"[{time.time() - t0:7.1f}s] queued {os.path.basename(path)}")
        except Exception as e:  # should not happen; keep going with what we have
            log(f"reader error: {type(e).__name__}: {e}")
        finally:
            reader_done.set()

    rt = threading.Thread(target=reader, daemon=True)
    rt.start()

    pending = {}  # (h, w) -> list of chunk messages
    n_pending = {}
    finished = 0
    frames_done = 0
    last_report = time.time()

    def finalize_ready(vid):
        nonlocal finished

"""Per-second object presence and people counts for FineVideo Parquet files.

Usage: python run.py --input <folder of .parquet files> --output results.jsonl

Default mode is the fast pipeline (parallel decode workers + TensorRT FP16 on
the GPU). `--mode simple` runs the first, single-process version (Ultralytics
predict) for comparison.
"""
import argparse
import json
import math
import os
import sys
import time

HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
sys.path.insert(0, HERE)

from vidx.aggregate import per_second  # noqa: E402
from vidx.parquet_io import iter_videos, list_parquet  # noqa: E402
from vidx.video import VideoReader  # noqa: E402


def effective_cpus():
    """CPUs we may actually use: affinity, limited by a cgroup CPU quota."""
    n = len(os.sched_getaffinity(0)) if hasattr(os, "sched_getaffinity") else os.cpu_count()
    try:
        quota, period = open("/sys/fs/cgroup/cpu.max").read().split()
        if quota != "max":
            n = min(n, math.ceil(int(quota) / int(period)))
    except (OSError, ValueError):
        pass
    return max(1, n)


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- simple mode
def process_video(vid, data, detector, per_sec, batch):
    """Return the output records for one video (never raises)."""
    seconds, counts, buf, buf_sec = [], [], [], []
    reader = VideoReader(data, per_second=per_sec)
    error = None

    def flush():
        if buf:
            counts.extend(detector.counts(buf))
            seconds.extend(buf_sec)
            buf.clear()
            buf_sec.clear()

    try:
        for sec, img in reader:
            buf.append(img)
            buf_sec.append(sec)
            if len(buf) >= batch:
                flush()
        flush()
    except Exception as e:
        error = f"could not decode video: {type(e).__name__}"
        try:
            flush()
        except Exception:
            buf.clear()
            buf_sec.clear()
    records = []
    if reader.last_second >= 0:
        for s, (objects, people) in enumerate(
            per_second(seconds[: len(counts)], counts, reader.last_second)
        ):
            records.append({"video": vid, "second": s, "objects": objects, "people": people})
    elif error is None:
        error = "no frames decoded"
    if error:
        records.append({"video": vid, "error": error})
    return records


def run_simple(args):
    from vidx.detect_ultra import UltralyticsDetector

    detector = UltralyticsDetector(args.weights, batch=32)
    t0 = time.time()
    n_videos = 0
    with open(args.output, "w") as out:
        for path in list_parquet(args.input):
            for vid, data, err in iter_videos(path):
                n_videos += 1
                if err:
                    records = [{"video": vid, "error": err}]
                else:
                    records = process_video(vid, data, detector, args.per_second, 32)
                for r in records:
                    out.write(json.dumps(r) + "\n")
                out.flush()
            print(f"[{time.time() - t0:8.1f}s] {os.path.basename(path)} done, "
                  f"{n_videos} videos", file=sys.stderr, flush=True)
    print(f"total {time.time() - t0:.1f}s for {n_videos} videos", file=sys.stderr)


# ------------------------------------------------------------------ fast mode
def run_fast(args):
    from vidx.engine import load_model
    from vidx.pipeline import log, run

    n_workers = args.workers or max(1, effective_cpus() - 1)
    log(f"workers: {n_workers}, frames/s analysed: {args.per_second}, "
        f"skip non-ref frames: {args.skip_nonref}")
    # start workers (fork) before CUDA is initialised in this process
    model = None

    def get_model():
        return load_model(args.weights, args.engine, log=log)

    run(args.input, args.output, model_factory=get_model, n_workers=n_workers,
        per_second_k=args.per_second, skip_nonref=args.skip_nonref,
        max_batch=args.batch, debug=args.debug)
    del model


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--input", required=True, help="folder of .parquet files")
    ap.add_argument("--output", required=True, help="output .jsonl path")
    ap.add_argument("--mode", choices=["fast", "simple"], default="fast")
    ap.add_argument("--weights", default=os.path.join(HERE, "yolo11l.pt"))
    ap.add_argument("--engine", default=os.path.join(HERE, "yolo11l.engine"))
    ap.add_argument("--per-second", type=int, default=3,
                    help="frames analysed per second (0 = every frame)")
    ap.add_argument("--skip-nonref", action="store_true",
                    help="do not decode non-reference (B) frames")
    ap.add_argument("--workers", type=int, default=0, help="decode processes (0 = auto)")
    ap.add_argument("--batch", type=int, default=64)
    ap.add_argument("--debug", action="store_true")
    args = ap.parse_args()
    if args.mode == "simple":
        run_simple(args)
    else:
        run_fast(args)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

Usage: python run.py --input <folder of .parquet files> --output results.jsonl

import json
import os
import sys
import time

from vidx.aggregate import per_second
from vidx.parquet_io import iter_videos, list_parquet
from vidx.video import VideoReader

HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))


def process_video(vid, data, detector, per_sec, batch):
    """Return the output records for one video (never raises)."""
    seconds, counts, buf, buf_sec = [], [], [], []

    error = None

        if buf:
            counts.extend(detector.counts(buf))
            seconds.extend(buf_sec)

        flush()
    except Exception as e:

"""Per-second object presence and people counts for FineVideo Parquet files.

Usage: python run.py --input <folder of .parquet files> --output results.jsonl

Default mode is the fast pipeline (parallel decode workers + TensorRT FP16 on
the GPU). `--mode simple` runs the first, single-process version (Ultralytics
predict) for comparison.
"""
import argparse
import json
import math
import os
import sys
import time

HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
sys.path.insert(0, HERE)

from vidx.aggregate import per_second  # noqa: E402
from vidx.parquet_io import iter_videos, list_parquet  # noqa: E402
from vidx.video import VideoReader  # noqa: E402


def effective_cpus():
    """CPUs we may actually use: affinity, limited by a cgroup CPU quota."""
    n = len(os.sched_getaffinity(0)) if hasattr(os, "sched_getaffinity") else os.cpu_count()
    try:
        quota, period = open("/sys/fs/cgroup/cpu.max").read().split()
        if quota != "max":
            n = min(n, math.ceil(int(quota) / int(period)))
    except (OSError, ValueError):
        pass
    return max(1, n)


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- simple mode
def process_video(vid, data, detector, per_sec, batch):
    """Return the output records for one video (never raises)."""
    seconds, counts, buf, buf_sec = [], [], [], []
    reader = VideoReader(data, per_second=per_sec)
    error = None

    def flush():
        if buf:
            counts.extend(detector.counts(buf))
            seconds.extend(buf_sec)
            buf.clear()
            buf_sec.clear()

    try:
        for sec, img in reader:
            buf.append(img)
            buf_sec.append(sec)
            if len(buf) >= batch:
                flush()
        flush()
    except Exception as e:
        error = f"could not decode video: {type(e).__name__}"
        try:
            flush()
        except Exception:
            buf.clear()
            buf_sec.clear()
    records = []
    if reader.last_second >= 0:
        for s, (objects, people) in enumerate(
            per_second(seconds[: len(counts)], counts, reader.last_second)
        ):
            records.append({"video": vid, "second": s, "objects": objects, "people": people})
    elif error is None:
        error = "no frames decoded"
    if error:
        records.append({"video": vid, "error": error})
    return records


def run_simple(args):
    from vidx.detect_ultra import UltralyticsDetector

    detector = UltralyticsDetector(args.weights, batch=32)
    t0 = time.time()
    n_videos = 0
    with open(args.output, "w") as out:
        for path in list_parquet(args.input):
            for vid, data, err in iter_videos(path):
                n_videos += 1
                if err:
                    records = [{"video": vid, "error": err}]
                else:
                    records = process_video(vid, data, detector, args.per_second, 32)
                for r in records:
                    out.write(json.dumps(r) + "\n")
                out.flush()
            print(f"[{time.time() - t0:8.1f}s] {os.path.basename(path)} done, "
                  f"{n_videos} videos", file=sys.stderr, flush=True)
    print(f"total {time.time() - t0:.1f}s for {n_videos} videos", file=sys.stderr)


# ------------------------------------------------------------------ fast mode
def run_fast(args):
    from vidx.engine import load_model
    from vidx.pipeline import log, run

    n_workers = args.workers or max(1, effective_cpus() - 1)
    log(f"workers: {n_workers}, frames/s analysed: {args.per_second}, "
        f"skip non-ref frames: {args.skip_nonref}")
    # start workers (fork) before CUDA is initialised in this process
    model = None

    def get_model():
        return load_model(args.weights, args.engine, log=log)

    run(args.input, args.output, model_factory=get_model, n_workers=n_workers,
        per_second_k=args.per_second, skip_nonref=args.skip_nonref,
        max_batch=args.batch, debug=args.debug)
    del model


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--input", required=True, help="folder of .parquet files")
    ap.add_argument("--output", required=True, help="output .jsonl path")
    ap.add_argument("--mode", choices=["fast", "simple"], default="fast")
    ap.add_argument("--weights", default=os.path.join(HERE, "yolo11l.pt"))
    ap.add_argument("--engine", default=os.path.join(HERE, "yolo11l.engine"))
    ap.add_argument("--per-second", type=int, default=3,
                    help="frames analysed per second (0 = every frame)")
    ap.add_argument("--skip-nonref", action="store_true",
                    help="do not decode non-reference (B) frames")
    ap.add_argument("--workers", type=int, default=0, help="decode processes (0 = auto)")
    ap.add_argument("--batch", type=int, default=64)
    ap.add_argument("--debug", action="store_true")
    args = ap.parse_args()
    if args.mode == "simple":
        run_simple(args)
    else:
        run_fast(args)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

input.content:
"""Decode worker process.

Each worker takes whole videos (mp4 bytes) from a task queue, decodes them
with PyAV on one core, keeps K frames per second (first frame in each
1/K-second slot), letterboxes them exactly like Ultralytics and writes them
into "chunks" in a shared-memory block owned by the main process. It then
sends a small message describing the chunk; the main process copies it to the
GPU and hands the chunk back through `free_q`.

Sequential sampling (odd K): frames in even slots (0, 2, 4, ...) are
"primary" and always analysed. Frames in odd slots are "deferred": they go to
separate chunks, each tagged with how many primary frames its second has, and
the main process analyses them only if the primary frames of that second
disagree. When ceil(K/2) primary frames agree on every class and on the people
count, the majority/median over all K frames is already decided, so the
result is identical to analysing all K.

Messages sent on `msg_q`:
  ("start", wid, vid)
  ("chunk", wid, chunk_id, vid, n, out_h, out_w, seconds, kind, n_primary)
      kind "p" (primary) or "d" (deferred); n_primary is a list for "d"
  ("end", wid, vid, last_second, n_decoded, error_or_None)
"""
import io
import math
import os
import traceback
from fractions import Fraction

import numpy as np

SLOT_BYTES = 640 * 640 * 3  # max letterboxed frame


class ChunkWriter:
    """Fills shared-memory chunks with letterboxed frames of one kind."""

    def __init__(self, kind, wid, vid, block, chunk_frames, free_q, msg_q, cv2, pad):
        self.kind, self.wid, self.vid = kind, wid, vid
        self.block, self.chunk_frames = block, chunk_frames
        self.free_q, self.msg_q, self.cv2, self.pad = free_q, msg_q, cv2, pad
        self.cid = None
        self.view = None
        self.geom = None
        self.geom_hw = None
        self.n = 0
        self.secs, self.extra = [], []

    def send(self):
        if self.cid is not None and self.n:
            g = self.geom
            self.msg_q.put(("chunk", self.wid, self.cid, self.vid, self.n, g[0], g[1],
                            self.secs, self.kind, self.extra if self.kind == "d" else None))
        elif self.cid is not None:
            self.free_q.put(self.cid)
        self.cid, self.view, self.n, self.secs, self.extra = None, None, 0, [], []

    def add(self, sec, img, geometry, extra=None, before_send=None):
        h, w = img.shape[:2]
        if self.geom_hw != (h, w):
            if self.n and before_send:
                before_send()
            self.send()  # never mix shapes in one chunk
            self.geom = geometry(h, w)
            self.geom_hw = (h, w)
        out_h, out_w, new_h, new_w, top, left = self.geom
        if self.cid is None:
            self.cid = self.free_q.get()
            self.view = self.block[self.cid, : self.chunk_frames * out_h * out_w * 3].reshape(
                self.chunk_frames, out_h, out_w, 3)
        dst = self.view[self.n]
        pad = self.pad
        if top:
            dst[:top] = pad
        if top + new_h < out_h:
            dst[top + new_h:] = pad
        if left:
            dst[:, :left] = pad
        if left + new_w < out_w:
            dst[:, left + new_w:] = pad
        area = dst[top:top + new_h, left:left + new_w]
        if (h, w) == (new_h, new_w):
            area[...] = img
        else:
            area[...] = self.cv2.resize(img, (new_w, new_h), interpolation=self.cv2.INTER_LINEAR)
        self.secs.append(sec)
        self.extra.append(extra)
        self.n += 1
        if self.n == self.chunk_frames:
            if before_send:
                before_send()
            self.send()


def worker_main(wid, task_q, msg_q, free_q, shm_name, n_chunks, chunk_frames, cfg):
    os.environ.setdefault("OMP_NUM_THREADS", "1")
    import av
    import cv2
    from multiprocessing import shared_memory

    from .letterbox import PAD, geometry
    from .video import _rotation_cw, rotate

    cv2.setNumThreads(1)
    av.logging.set_level(av.logging.PANIC)  # damaged files: no log spam
    shm = shared_memory.SharedMemory(name=shm_name)
    block = np.ndarray((n_chunks, chunk_frames * SLOT_BYTES), np.uint8, shm.buf)
    k = cfg["per_second"]
    skip_nonref = cfg.get("skip_nonref", False)
    sequential = bool(cfg.get("sequential")) and k >= 3 and k % 2 == 1

    while True:
        task = task_q.get()
        if task is None:
            break
        vid, data = task
        msg_q.put(("start", wid, vid))

            out_h, out_w, new_h, new_w, top, left = g
            if state["chunk"] is None:
                cid = free_q.get()
                state["chunk"] = cid
                state["view"] = block[cid, : chunk_frames * out_h * out_w * 3].reshape(
                    chunk_frames, out_h, out_w, 3)
            dst = state["view"][state["n"]]
            # grey padding strips, then the image
            if top:
                dst[:top] = PAD
            if top + new_h < out_h:
                dst[top + new_h:] = PAD
            if left:
                dst[:, :left] = PAD
            if left + new_w < out_w:
                dst[:, left + new_w:] = PAD
            area = dst[top:top + new_h, left:left + new_w]
            if (h, w) == (new_h, new_w):
                area[...] = img
            else:
                area[...] = cv2.resize(img, (new_w, new_h), interpolation=cv2.INTER_LINEAR)
            state["secs"].append(sec)
            state["n"] += 1
            if state["n"] == chunk_frames:
                send_chunk()

        last_second, n_decoded, error = -1, 0, None
        try:
            container = av.open(io.BytesIO(data), mode="r", metadata_errors="ignore")
            try:
                if not container.streams.video:
                    raise ValueError("no video stream")
                stream = container.streams.video[0]
                cc = stream.codec_context
                if skip_nonref:
                    cc.skip_frame = "NONREF"
                tb = stream.time_base or Fraction(1, 1000)
                fps = float(stream.average_rate or stream.guessed_rate or 30)
                first_pts, max_pkt_pts, rot, last_slot = None, None, None, None
                for packet in container.demux(stream):
                    if packet.pts is not None and (max_pkt_pts is None or packet.pts > max_pkt_pts):
                        max_pkt_pts = packet.pts
                    for frame in packet.decode():
                        idx = n_decoded
                        n_decoded += 1
                        if frame.pts is not None:
                            if first_pts is None:
                                first_pts = frame.pts
                            t = (frame.pts - first_pts) * tb
                        else:
                            t = Fraction(idx) / Fraction(fps)
                        if t < 0:
                            t = Fraction(0)
                        sec = math.floor(t)
                        if sec > last_second:
                            last_second = sec
                        if k:
                            slot = (sec, math.floor((t - sec) * k))
                            if slot == last_slot:
                                continue
                            last_slot = slot
                        if rot is None:
                            rot = _rotation_cw(stream, frame)
                        img = frame.to_ndarray(format="bgr24")
                        add_frame(sec, rotate(img, rot))
                if skip_nonref and first_pts is not None and max_pkt_pts is not None:
                    # skipped B-frames may lie after the last decoded frame
                    last_second = max(last_second, math.floor((max_pkt_pts - first_pts) * tb))
            finally:
                container.close()
        except Exception as e:
            error = f"could not decode video: {type(e).__name__}"
            if cfg.get("debug"):
                traceback.print_exc()
        send_chunk()
        if n_decoded == 0 and error is None:
            error = "no frames decoded"
        msg_q.put(("end", wid, vid, last_second, n_decoded, error))
    shm.close()

"""Fast pipeline: parallel decode workers -> shared memory -> one GPU loop.

Main process:
  - a reader thread reads Parquet files in order and puts (video id, mp4
    bytes) on the task queue (error rows go straight to the output);
  - N worker processes decode/sample/letterbox into shared-memory chunks
    (see worker.py);
  - the main thread batches frames of the same shape, runs YOLO on the GPU,
    counts the five classes per frame, decides which deferred frames are
    needed (sequential sampling), and writes each video's lines as soon as it
    is complete;
  - a worker that dies (e.g. a decoder crash on a damaged file) is replaced,
    and its current video gets an error line.
"""
import json
import multiprocessing as mp
import os
import queue
import sys
import threading
import time
from collections import defaultdict
from multiprocessing import shared_memory

import numpy as np

from .aggregate import per_second
from .parquet_io import iter_videos, list_parquet
from .worker import SLOT_BYTES, worker_main


def log(*a):
    print(*a, file=sys.stderr, flush=True)


class VideoState:
    __slots__ = ("secs", "counts", "chunks_sent", "chunks_done", "end", "prim", "waiting")

    def __init__(self):
        self.secs, self.counts = [], []
        self.chunks_sent = self.chunks_done = 0
        self.end = None  # (last_second, n_decoded, error)
        self.prim = defaultdict(list)  # second -> [(presence bytes, people)] of primaries
        self.waiting = []  # deferred chunks not yet fully decided


def records_for(vid, st):
    last_second, _, error = st.end
    recs = []
    if last_second >= 0:
        secs = np.concatenate(st.secs) if st.secs else np.zeros(0, np.int64)
        counts = np.concatenate(st.counts) if st.counts else np.zeros((0, 5), np.int32)
        for s, (objects, people) in enumerate(per_second(secs, counts, last_second)):
            recs.append({"video": vid, "second": s, "objects": objects, "people": people})
    if error:
        recs.append({"video": vid, "error": error})
    return recs


class Deferred:
    """A deferred chunk waiting for its seconds' primary results."""
    __slots__ = ("msg", "need", "decided", "n_undecided")

    def __init__(self, msg):
        self.msg = msg
        n = msg[4]
        self.need = [None] * n
        self.n_undecided = n


def run(input_dir, output_path, model_factory, n_workers, per_second_k=3, skip_nonref=False,
        sequential=True, max_batch=64, chunk_frames=32, chunks_per_worker=6, debug=False):
    import torch

    from .postprocess import count_classes

    # forkserver: workers are forked from a clean single-threaded server, so a
    # worker restarted mid-run does not inherit CUDA or thread locks.
    ctx = mp.get_context("forkserver")
    ctx.set_forkserver_preload(["av", "cv2", "numpy", "vidx.worker"])
    t0 = time.time()
    out = open(output_path, "w")
    need_primary = (per_second_k + 1) // 2
    cfg = {"per_second": per_second_k, "skip_nonref": skip_nonref, "debug": debug,
           "sequential": sequential}
    task_q = ctx.Queue(maxsize=max(4, n_workers))
    msg_q = ctx.Queue()
    workers = {}  # wid -> dict(proc, free_q, shm, block, current)

    def start_worker(wid):
        shm = shared_memory.SharedMemory(create=True,
                                         size=chunks_per_worker * chunk_frames * SLOT_BYTES)
        block = np.ndarray((chunks_per_worker, chunk_frames * SLOT_BYTES), np.uint8, shm.buf)
        free_q = ctx.SimpleQueue()
        for c in range(chunks_per_worker):
            free_q.put(c)
        p = ctx.Process(target=worker_main, daemon=True,
                        args=(wid, task_q, msg_q, free_q, shm.name, chunks_per_worker,
                              chunk_frames, cfg))
        p.start()
        workers[wid] = dict(proc=p, free_q=free_q, shm=shm, block=block, current=None)

    videos = {}  # vid -> VideoState
    reader_done = threading.Event()
    n_tasks = [0]
    direct_errors = queue.Queue()  # rows that failed before decoding

    def reader():
        try:
            for path in list_parquet(input_dir):
                for vid, data, err in iter_videos(path):
                    if err:
                        direct_errors.put({"video": vid, "error": err})
                        continue
                    n_tasks[0] += 1
                    task_q.put((vid, data))
                if debug:
                    log(f"[{time.time() - t0:7.1f}s] queued {os.path.basename(path)}")
        except Exception as e:  # should not happen; keep going with what we have
            log(f"reader error: {type(e).__name__}: {e}")
        finally:
            reader_done.set()

    # Start reading and decoding first; load the model while they work.
    rt = threading.Thread(target=reader, daemon=True)
    rt.start()
    for wid in range(n_workers):
        start_worker(wid)
    model = model_factory()
    log(f"[{time.time() - t0:7.1f}s] model ready")

    pending = defaultdict(list)  # (h, w) -> items (wid, cid, idx|None, n, vid, secs, kind, ref)
    n_pending = defaultdict(int)
    stats = {"finished": 0, "frames": 0, "deferred_total": 0, "deferred_run": 0}
    last_report = time.time()

    def finalize_ready(vid):
        st = videos.get(vid)
        if st is not None and st.end is not None and st.chunks_done == st.chunks_sent:
            out.write("".join(json.dumps(r) + "\n" for r in records_for(vid, st)))
            del videos[vid]
            stats["finished"] += 1

    def enqueue(item, h, w):
        pending[(h, w)].append(item)
        n_pending[(h, w)] += item[3]

    def try_decide(st, d):
        """Decide deferred frames whose seconds have all their primaries."""
        _, wid, cid, vid, n, h, w, secs, _, n_prim = d.msg
        for i in range(n):
            if d.need[i] is not None:
                continue
            got = st.prim.get(secs[i], ())
            if n_prim[i] < need_primary:
                d.need[i] = True
            elif len(got) >= n_prim[i]:
                first = got[0]
                d.need[i] = any(g != first for g in got)
            else:
                continue
            d.n_undecided -= 1
        if d.n_undecided:
            return False
        idx = np.flatnonzero(d.need)
        stats["deferred_total"] += n
        stats["deferred_run"] += len(idx)
        if len(idx):
            enqueue((wid, cid, idx, len(idx), vid, [secs[i] for i in idx], "d", None), h, w)
        else:
            workers[wid]["free_q"].put(cid)
            st.chunks_done += 1
        return True

    def handle(msg):
        kind = msg[0]
        if kind == "start":
            _, wid, vid = msg
            workers[wid]["current"] = vid
            videos.setdefault(vid, VideoState())
        elif kind == "chunk":
            _, wid, cid, vid, n, h, w, secs, ckind, _ = msg
            st = videos[vid]
            st.chunks_sent += 1
            if ckind == "p":
                enqueue((wid, cid, None, n, vid, secs, "p", None), h, w)
            else:
                d = Deferred(msg)
                if not try_decide(st, d):
                    st.waiting.append(d)
        elif kind == "end":
            _, wid, vid, last_second, n_decoded, error = msg
            workers[wid]["current"] = None
            videos[vid].end = (last_second, n_decoded, error)
            finalize_ready(vid)

    def run_batch(shape):
        h, w = shape
        items, total = [], 0
        lst = pending[shape]
        while lst and total < max_batch:
            it = lst.pop(0)
            items.append(it)
            total += it[3]
        n_pending[shape] -= total
        parts = []
        for (wid, cid, idx, n, vid, secs, kind, _) in items:
            view = workers[wid]["block"][cid]
            if idx is None:
                arr = view[: n * h * w * 3].reshape(n, h, w, 3)
            else:
                arr = view[: (int(idx[-1]) + 1) * h * w * 3].reshape(-1, h, w, 3)[idx]
            parts.append(torch.from_numpy(arr).to("cuda"))
            workers[wid]["free_q"].put(cid)
        x = torch.cat(parts) if len(parts) > 1 else parts[0]
        x = x.permute(0, 3, 1, 2).flip(1).float().div_(255)  # BGR->RGB, 0..1
        counts = []
        for i in range(0, x.shape[0], model.max_batch):
            counts.append(count_classes(model(x[i:i + model.max_batch])))
        counts = torch.cat(counts).cpu().numpy()
        off = 0
        touched = set()
        for (wid, cid, idx, n, vid, secs, kind, _) in items:
            st = videos[vid]
            c = counts[off:off + n]
            off += n
            st.secs.append(np.asarray(secs, np.int64))
            st.counts.append(c)
            st.chunks_done += 1
            if kind == "p":
                pres = c > 0
                for j, s in enumerate(secs):
                    st.prim[s].append((pres[j].tobytes(), int(c[j, 0])))
                touched.add(vid)
            else:
                finalize_ready(vid)
        for vid in touched:
            st = videos[vid]
            if st.waiting:
                st.waiting = [d for d in st.waiting if not try_decide(st, d)]
            finalize_ready(vid)
        stats["frames"] += total

    def check_workers():
        for wid, wk in list(workers.items()):
            if wk["proc"].is_alive():
                continue
            vid = wk["current"]
            log(f"worker {wid} died (exit {wk['proc'].exitcode}) on {vid}; restarting")
            # finish the work it already handed over (its memory is ours)
            for st in list(videos.values()):
                for d in st.waiting:
                    if d.msg[1] == wid:
                        d.need = [True if x is None else x for x in d.need]
                        d.n_undecided = 0
                        try_decide(st, d)
                st.waiting = [d for d in st.waiting if d.n_undecided]
            while True:
                shapes = [sh for sh, lst in pending.items() if any(it[0] == wid for it in lst)]
                if not shapes:
                    break
                run_batch(shapes[0])
            if vid is not None and vid in videos:
                st = videos[vid]
                secs = np.concatenate(st.secs) if st.secs else np.zeros(0, np.int64)
                st.end = (int(secs.max()) if len(secs) else -1, 0,
                          "could not decode video: decoder crashed")
                finalize_ready(vid)
            wk["shm"].close()
            wk["shm"].unlink()
            del workers[wid]
            start_worker(wid)

    try:
        while True:
            while not direct_errors.empty():
                out.write(json.dumps(direct_errors.get()) + "\n")
            got = False
            try:
                msg = msg_q.get(timeout=0.002 if any(n_pending.values()) else 0.05)
                handle(msg)
                got = True
                while True:  # drain without blocking
                    handle(msg_q.get_nowait())
            except queue.Empty:
                pass
            # run a batch if any shape has a full batch, or if nothing new arrived
            ready = [s for s, n in n_pending.items() if n >= max_batch]
            if not ready and not got:
                ready = [s for s, n in n_pending.items() if n > 0]
            if ready:
                run_batch(max(ready, key=lambda s: n_pending[s]))
            elif not got:
                check_workers()
                if reader_done.is_set() and direct_errors.empty() \
                        and stats["finished"] >= n_tasks[0] and not videos:
                    break
            if debug and time.time() - last_report > 30:
                el = time.time() - t0
                log(f"[{el:7.1f}s] videos done {stats['finished']}, frames {stats['frames']} "
                    f"({stats['frames'] / el:.0f}/s)")
                last_report = time.time()
    finally:
        for _ in workers:
            try:
                task_q.put_nowait(None)
            except Exception:
                pass
        for wk in workers.values():
            wk["proc"].join(timeout=5)
            if wk["proc"].is_alive():
                wk["proc"].kill()
            wk["shm"].close()
            try:
                wk["shm"].unlink()
            except FileNotFoundError:
                pass
        out.close()
    log(f"done: {stats['finished']} videos, {stats['frames']} frames analysed "
        f"(deferred run {stats['deferred_run']}/{stats['deferred_total']}) "
        f"in {time.time() - t0:.1f}s")
